seo.title: Fisheries Monitoring Capacity, KAMAMKUKI JCMA | Oceans Alive Foundation
seo.description: A two phase programme turning five Beach Management Units across two counties into a single, evidence led system for monitoring and defending shared fisheries.

hero.title: Fisheries Monitoring Capacity, KAMAMKUKI JCMA
hero.text: With funding from Blue Ventures Conservation, Oceans Alive is strengthening fisheries monitoring and co-management across five Beach Management Units.

geographyBand.text3: Together these five Beach Management Units manage roughly 304 square kilometres of coastal and marine waters within Kenya's territorial sea, alongside the Kenya Fisheries Service and their respective county governments.

overview.heading: Reliable Data for a Resource Under Pressure
overview.text: The JCMA faces a familiar set of pressures: destructive and illegal fishing, declining fish stocks, habitat degradation, weak enforcement, and thin institutional capacity within the co-management bodies meant to hold the line.
overview.text2: The response is built around governance and institutional development, fisheries catch and ecological monitoring, compliance strengthening, financial resilience for fishing households, and community food security, delivered under Kenya's Fisheries Management and Development Act No. 35 of 2016. Delivery combines ongoing fisheries data collection, community resource surveys, data feedback sessions, compliance assessments, exchange visits, stakeholder engagement and technical partnerships, aimed at systems that keep working long after the project ends.

twoPhaseBuild.heading: Building the System in Two Stages
twoPhaseBuild.text2: Diagnosed and closed governance and institutional capacity gaps across all five BMUs, and stood up a fisheries catch monitoring system at ten landing sites within the JCMA.
twoPhaseBuild.text4: Adds structured BMU governance mentorship, peer learning between BMUs, Village Savings and Loan Associations for financial resilience, and deeper fisheries and ecological monitoring.

collaboration.heading: One Table, Five BMUs and Their Governments
collaboration.text: Oceans Alive and Blue Ventures work closely with the five BMUs, the KAMAMKUKI Joint Co-Management Area Committee, national and county government institutions, and research organisations. The aim is a stronger, better coordinated co-management system: capable BMUs, reliable fisheries information, improved compliance, greater community financial resilience, and partnerships built to last beyond the project itself.

callToAction.heading: Help Strengthen Fisheries Governance
callToAction.text: Your support helps BMUs monitor and manage shared fisheries resources for the long term.
